protocol.training: None; no fit, calibrator fit, model selection, ablation fit or test optimization.
protocol.permutations: Declared in source: 12 paired-column permutations each of geography and season, seed 42; temporal and geographic validation only; no outcome-dependent choice.
protocol.explanations: Existing backend.predict.explain: calibrated-probability permutation SHAP, 16 saved background rows, seed 42, four permutations per explanation.
protocol.ap: Average precision, not trapezoidal PR area; tied-score precision contributions sum to AP.
protocol.dependence: County-days are not independent events. Calendar-week bootstrap preserves spatial rows; intervals are descriptive.
protocol.candidate_limit: Only selected and frozen baseline model objects are saved; other candidate validation metrics are used as recorded, never refitted.

paired_uncertainty.method: 300 paired calendar-week block resamples; spatial rows within week retained; descriptive 95% interval

selection.warning: Row-weighted mean AP is not pooled AP. Sensitivity deletes one positive row; prevalence changes. No model is reselected.

noaa_records.EVENT_NARRATIVE: Thunderstorm wind gusts up to 81 MPH were reported at the Saddle Peak sensor.
noaa_records.EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A very powerful winter storm brought heavy rain, strong thunderstorms and gusty winds to Southwestern California Rainfall totals generally ranged from 1.50 to 4.00 inches across coastal and valley areas with 3.00 to 7.00 inches across the foothills and mountains with significant snowfall at the higher elevations. With this rainfall, numerous reports of flash flooding were received. Strong thunderstorms were also observed, resulting in strong outflow winds and wind damage.

noaa_records.EVENT_NARRATIVE: The Huntington SW mesonet station recorded a wind gust of 61 mph as a result of outflow winds associated with a nearby cluster of showers and thunderstorms moving through the area.
noaa_records.EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A grazing shortwave trough north of Utah sent a cold front into the region. Ahead of and along this boundary there was enough moisture to result in isolated to scattered convective development, with much of this activity higher based in nature. As a result, numerous strong to severe wind gusts were recorded or reported. Additionally, a period of strong winds downsloping off of terrain was noted in portions of northwest Utah following the passage of the frontal boundary.
